reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: delegated to the core Integration service and its connection/attempt state

reviewedPartitions.inputs: PTY id and location scope, the x-opencode-ticket: 1 token-mint header, optional short-lived ticket and replay cursor query values, plus WebSocket text or binary terminal input frames
reviewedPartitions.outputs: a scoped one-time connect token or a WebSocket stream that emits bounded replay chunks, an absolute-cursor control frame and live PTY output while forwarding valid UTF-8 client input to the attached PTY
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: token mint rejects a missing or invalid CSRF header/origin with ForbiddenError and a missing PTY with PtyNotFoundError; connect rejects a missing pre-upgrade PTY with 404 and an invalid/disallowed ticket with 403; post-upgrade missing/exited attach closes with code 4404; invalid UTF-8 binary input is dropped; socket close/errors terminate the transport path while detach is ensured
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: tickets live in a global cache for at most 60 seconds and are consumed atomically once only when ptyID/directory/workspaceID scope matches; each WebSocket attachment lives until the socket/drain race ends and is detached in finalization
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: ticket state is capped at 10,000 entries and replay strings are split at 65,536 JavaScript string units per frame, but the server WebSocket outbox is explicitly unbounded and graceful-shutdown socket tracking remains a TODO, so an end-to-end bounded native transport lifetime is not established
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The six residual INT rows remain one generic source-indistinguishable class. Core PTY/ticket paths also overlap the already accepted opencode.process-terminal owners, while the server transport requires HTTP/WebSocket/auth authority and still has an unbounded outbox plus unresolved graceful-shutdown tracking. No residual INT id can own this boundary by subtraction.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: one authoritative HttpApi/ClientApi contract plus explicit product group/endpoint naming and omission policy; runtime Promise clients take base URL, optional fetch/headers and per-request abort/header options
reviewedPartitions.outputs: committed Promise and imported-Effect client source generated from the same compiled operation set, with structural wire values for Promise and decoded Effect-native values for Effect
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: generation fails closed on required client middleware without an adapter, ambiguous/multiple schemas, naming collisions, unsupported or unportable shapes and unsafe output paths; Promise runtime preserves declared tagged errors and normalizes transport, status, content-type and malformed-response failures to stable ClientError reasons
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: code generation is build-time; a private manifest tracks only files owned by the generator so stale generated files can be removed without deleting unrelated files; runtime client state is per client/stream and generated streams do not reconnect automatically
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: the product build emits Promise and Effect outputs with concurrency two; Promise SSE parsing caps its accumulated string buffer at 1,048,576 JavaScript string units and cancels/releases the reader on exit; network lifetime belongs to the supplied fetch/HttpClient transport
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The generator is generic infrastructure and its own spec says OpenCode owns product endpoint filtering before generation. Product caller/tests still map to the same broad integration/server-control-plane surfaces, including already implemented INT-008 behavior. Generated-client evidence therefore cannot distinguish one of the six residual INT ids or imply ownership of the separate sdks/** remainder.

reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: project cache reads are best-effort and resolution falls back deterministically; project cache commit ignores write failure by design; invalid session IDs become InvalidRequestError, missing sessions become SessionNotFoundError and session database read defects die; malformed percent-encoded directory headers fall back to the raw header text
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: ProjectV2.resolve reads but does not mutate the repo-local project cache; commit is a temporary bridge after old-service migration/persistence; request location context is request-scoped while session context remains pinned in the session row; the underlying core Location runtime has separate configuration-runtime ownership
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: project resolution performs filesystem and git discovery/remote/history reads; request middleware itself is request-scoped while session middleware also reads database state; location-scoped runtime lifetime is delegated to the separately owned core Location runtime rather than established by this integration boundary
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: ProjectV2 explicitly leaves database migration/persistence to the old service, placing commit-side effects next to frozen INT-002 repository ownership, and no genuine spec defines its remote/cache/root/global identity precedence. Core location services are separately mapped to configuration-runtime owners, while cross-location EventV2 compatibility overlaps frozen implemented INT-008. The six residual INT rows remain task-indistinguishable, so this protocol/context boundary cannot select one owner.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: VS Code command invocations, visible/active terminal state and the active editor file/selection within a workspace folder
reviewedPartitions.outputs: focus of an existing opencode terminal or creation of a split VS Code terminal that launches the opencode CLI on a random port, plus optional localhost prompt append and @file#line-range context injection
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: missing editor/workspace/active terminal context is a no-op; startup probe fetch failures are swallowed and prompt injection is skipped after ten unsuccessful probes; append-prompt fetch failures propagate; no explicit port-collision recovery or HTTP timeout is defined
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: command registrations live in the VS Code extension subscription scope; the selected random port is stored in terminal environment metadata; deactivate is empty and terminal/process lifetime remains owned by VS Code rather than the extension
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: the bridge owns IDE UI access, terminal creation, CLI command launch, terminal environment injection, 200 ms readiness delays and localhost HTTP fetches; fetches have no explicit timeout/abort and no direct automated extension behavior test exists at the locked pin
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: This is the literal sdks/** integration surface, but it requires VS Code UI state, terminal/process execution, environment injection and localhost network authority that are outside a bounded native residual INT contract. The source/spec/caller chain has no direct automated behavior test, and the six residual INT rows provide no task-specific binding.

reviewedPartitions.inputs: registered key/OAuth/env authentication methods, raw key material or OAuth inputs/code, stored credential connections, provider authorize/refresh callbacks and process environment values
reviewedPartitions.outputs: credential-backed or env-backed active connections; stored key/OAuth credentials; OAuth attempt status transitions; refreshed OAuth credential material; Integration.Updated and ConnectionUpdated events after committed credential changes
reviewedPartitions.failureSemantics: provider authorize/refresh/callback failures are wrapped as AuthorizationError; missing key/OAuth methods and missing/already-completing attempts die as defects; code-mode completion without a code returns CodeRequiredError; failed attempts retain a squashed message until terminal retention expires; environment resolution returns undefined when the variable is absent
reviewedPartitions.stateLifetime: pending OAuth attempts expire after 10 minutes, completed/failed/expired terminal status is retained for 1 minute, a scrubber runs every 30 seconds, auto callbacks execute in the attempt scope, and cancel/settle/expiry close that scope; stored credentials outlive attempts in Credential.Service
reviewedPartitions.resourceLifetime: the attempt map has time-based cleanup but no explicit concurrent-attempt capacity bound; auto provider callbacks run in background fibers; provider authorize/refresh callbacks may own external network/browser resources; env connections read process state; successful key/OAuth flows mutate credential storage and publish events
reviewedPartitions.ownershipBlocker: The dedicated opencode.integration-auth surface already maps this source to accepted PROV-007/008/010 and SEC-009 plus locally implemented EXT-007 and INT-004. Those local implementations intentionally exclude raw secrets, env access, provider callback/refresh execution, persistence, events and network. No genuine pinned spec defines the 10-minute/1-minute/30-second/5-minute lifecycle constants, refresh has no direct Integration service test, and the upstream attempt map has no explicit concurrency cap. The six generic residual INT rows therefore cannot re-own this authority by broad-surface overlap.

closureCriteria: Each residual INT owner requires task-specific source, caller, direct test and genuine spec evidence that distinguishes it from the six-row equivalence class; task number, controller status and generated endpoint order are insufficient.
Any network/transport candidate must explicitly own credentials, authentication, reconnect/timeout/failure behavior and resource lifetime and must not re-own INT-004 or frozen INT-008 behavior.
INT-002 remains frozen for repository side effects and INT-010 remains governed by the enterprise-remote missing-spec record unless materially new pinned evidence resolves those blockers.

The PTY WebSocket/ticket boundary remains blocked until task-specific evidence distinguishes a residual INT owner and explicitly resolves the unbounded outbox, graceful-shutdown lifetime and server auth/network authority without re-owning accepted process-terminal behavior.

Project/location ownership remains blocked until task-specific evidence separates pure identity/context resolution from legacy migration/persistence, the configuration-runtime Location graph and frozen EventV2 compatibility, with explicit filesystem/git/database authority and lifetime bounds.

The sdks/vscode bridge remains blocked until a direct automated extension behavior test and task-specific owner exist and an approved native boundary explicitly owns IDE/terminal/process-environment/localhost-network authority plus timeout, cancellation and cleanup semantics.

Executable integration-auth behavior remains closed to residual INT ownership unless new task-specific evidence both distinguishes an owner from the fully accounted integration-auth surface and explicitly grants secret storage, process-environment, provider callback/refresh, event and network/browser authority with bounded concurrent attempt resources and specified lifecycle constants.
All reviewed and unresolved rule partitions must receive source-grounded task dispositions or remain blocked before the integrations family can be called decomposed.
